look_here_first: Start low on the plant. Gray goldenrod is comparatively short and gray-hairy, with a densely pubescent stem and narrow spatulate-to-oblanceolate lower leaves that become smaller and narrower upward. Then check the usually one-sided, wandlike/recurving flowering branches.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: usually shorter and less colony-forming than tall goldenrods

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaves oblanceolate to spatulate and narrowed into a winged petiole

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper leaves progressively smaller and narrower

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowering array often one-sided and wandlike or recurving

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: common in dry open prairie, caliche, glade, old-field, and roadside settings

lookalikes.differences: Compared with Solidago radula, S. nemoralis is more gray/strigose overall and usually has a more wandlike one-sided inflorescence; S. radula is conspicuously scabrous with broader lower leaves and a more compact terminal panicle.
